label: Keep File
description: Make a file this run stored outlive the run. A run's files are walled per run: they are swept when the run ends, and no other run can read them even before that. `scope: execution` (the default) only extends how long THIS run's file lives; it is still unreadable from any other run. `scope: project` copies the file into the project's storage and emits the NEW reference, which every later run of the project can read: this is how an upload received in one request is served by the next. `ttl_days` is how long the kept file lives once nobody touches it, in either scope. Wire the emitted `file` into whatever stores or uses it later. For a file that is not in storage yet (a URL), use FetchToStorage instead.

inputs.name: file
inputs.description: Stored execution file (any type). With `scope: execution` it is the file that gets kept; with `scope: project` it is the file that gets copied, and it stays where it was.

inputs.name: scope
inputs.label: Keep as
inputs.description: `execution`: flag this run's file to survive the end-of-run sweep for `ttl_days`; only this run can ever read it. `project`: copy it into the project scope so every later run can read it, living for `ttl_days` (until deleted when empty).

inputs.name: ttl_days
inputs.label: Keep for (days, 0 = forever)
inputs.description: How long the kept file lives once nobody touches it: any access (download, read, presign) resets the clock, and 0 means never expire. Empty means the storage default of 30 days for an execution file, and no expiry for a project copy.

outputs.name: file
outputs.description: With `scope: execution`, the same reference, now flagged to survive the run. With `scope: project`, the reference to the NEW project-scoped copy (same filename, mime type and size); read this one from later runs.

outputs.name: filename
outputs.description: The name the file is stored under.
